overview.overview:
Kansas has voted Republican in every presidential election since 1968, and recent results confirm its place well to the right of the nation. The state backed the Republican by about 15 points in 2020 and by roughly 16 points in 2024, giving it a lean of about 16 points versus the country as a whole. With the national environment favoring Republicans by nearly five points, the expected margin here is about 11 points Republican, a modest improvement for Democrats relative to recent cycles but still a comfortable Republican hold.

Kansas carries six electoral votes and is not considered competitive at the tipping-point level. The wide uncertainty band reflects the absence of state polling rather than genuine competitiveness, spanning from a 20-point Republican win to a narrow 2-point one.
overview.watch: A strong Democratic national swing could bring the margin into single digits, but Kansas would still require an unusually large shift to become genuinely contested.
key_factors: A consistent double-digit Republican lean across the last two presidential cycles
A national environment tilted about five points toward Republicans
No available state polling, widening the uncertainty range
